strategies.text:
Overview

Mega Raichu Y is an excellent addition to Electric themed battle parties with its ability to DPS in small windows and potential power in Zap Cannon+. Due to its very fragile and mostly non-threatening movesets this solo is quite simple.

Est Time to Win: 170.5s - 210.5s

Main Strategy

Utilizing Primal Groudon, comfortably DPS Mega Raichu per cycle until Primal Groudon requires healing. Be mindful to exit the fight without having leftover energy as this would lower DPS significantly if repeated too often.


Mega Raichu Y has 1 counter point to Primal Groudon in learning Surf. As a result if it learns Surf, it is recommended to add additional ground attackers. Lots of damage & energy will be absorbed from surf so it is wise to not over extend using each attacker. A recommended strategy is swapping to the next attacker when below 25-30% health.

Overview

Mega Raichu Y's frailty makes it much easier to beat compared to its X counterpart. Conveniently so, Mega Raichu Y is better in terms of an Attacker than X. So as expected for an Electric Raid Boss, you'll want a strong Ground attacker.

And what better Ground attacker than Garchomp? With its Ground/Dragon typing giving strong defense and its really good Attack giving strong offense, it's the perfect counter. You don't even need to Mega Evolve it or XL it.

Gible Community Day is also coming soon, and with it a perfect opportunity to get a Garchomp and start walloping these recharging rats.

Est Time to Win

290-300 seconds

Main Strategy

Recycle, recycle, recycle, and you guessed it; recycle. Also be sure to relobby before your Pokémon faints so you can save time and Revives from the relobby.

strategies.strategyName: The Hazing of Mega Raichu Y by the Coward Necrozma Dawn Wings
strategies.text:
Overview

Mega Raichu Y is an incredibly strong pick for Electric-type counters, with the introduction of Plus Moves turning it into an absolute powerhouse that, at the time of writing is rivaled only by its lesser alphabetic cousin, Mega Raichu X, for both solo and duo configurations.

However, what it gains in power, it absolutely does not in bulk—to the extent that strong neutral attackers such as Mega Rayquaza, and for the purposes of this guide, Dawn Wings, can solo it. With a small loan from the weather gods, that is.

Fun fact: This solo was done in transboundary haze conditions, rather than actual fog (but to the game, they are one and the same, apparently, which presents us with an opportunity).

Est Time to Win: 285-295 seconds.


Main Strategy

A full team of Necrozma Dawn Wings should ensure you get the job done. There is a balance to be struck between going with Shadow Claw or Psycho Cut; the former frontloads damage into Dawn Wings's fast moves, which help given the 20% weather boost. The latter generates Moongeist Beam faster, but requires a bit more engagement; you should ideally be Tick Perfect Casting (TPC).

In terms of reactive strategy, Raichu's Surf is less of an issue for Dawn Wings than standard Ground-type counters, but this does not mean it can tank Surf repeatedly. Dawn Wings can tank up to 3, but that leaves it at risk of fainting to chip damage from Raichu Y's fast moves. Therefore, it is recommended that you tank 2, and dodge from the 3rd Surf onwards.
